svg.title: Vesalius's Human Dissection Corrections (De Humani Corporis Fabrica, 1543)
svg.desc: Edexcel GCSE History anatomical comparison diagram illustrating Andreas Vesalius's 1543 corrections from direct human dissection in Padua: a single fused mandible bone, a three-part human sternum, a thick solid cardiac septum with zero pores, a smooth two-lobed human liver, and absence of the animal rete mirabile in humans.
svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY · RENAISSANCE SCIENTIFIC OBSERVATION (1543)
Vesalius's Human Dissection Corrections (De Humani Corporis Fabrica, 1543)

g.text: R. LOBE
L. LOBE
CORRECTION 1 · MANDIBLE
Single Fused Human Mandible Bone
Inspecting real human skulls proved the adult lower jaw is
a single continuous fused bone — overturning Galen's
ape- and dog-based claim of two separate jawbones.
HOW VESALIUS PROVED IT (PADUA)
Hands-On Human Dissection
Stepping down from the lecturer's chair, Vesalius performed
dissections himself on executed criminals supplied by a
sympathetic Padua judge, testing every claim by eye.
CORRECTION 3 · HEART WALL
Thick, Solid Muscular Septum — Zero Pores
Proved the cardiac septum is dense, solid muscle with
zero pores: blood cannot seep directly from the right
ventricle to the left — paving the way for Harvey (1628).
TURNING POINT · 1543 FABRICA
Scientific Revolution in Anatomy
• 300+ Errors Corrected: Proved Galen had described
pigs and apes rather than human beings.
• Britain Impact (1545): Thomas Geminus printed the
Compendiosa in London, training English barber-surgeons.
• Limit: Improved anatomical map & surgery, though
it did not yet explain infectious disease causes.
CRANIAL CORRECTION · BASE OF BRAIN
No Rete Mirabile in Humans
Dissecting human heads, Vesalius proved the animal
rete mirabile blood network does not exist in humans —
calling out his own earlier student belief in Galen's myth.
• Mapped true human cerebral arteries (later named the
Circle of Willis) feeding the brain directly.
CORRECTION 2 · BREASTBONE
Three-Part Human Sternum
Demonstrated the adult human breastbone has only three
parts (manubrium, fused body & xiphoid), not
the seven separate segments found in apes.
TECHNOLOGY + ART (1440s PRESS & RENAISSANCE ART)
270+ Woodcuts & Mass Printing
Renaissance artists (Titian's studio / Calcar) drew exact
plates; the printing press spread copies across Europe.
CORRECTION 4 · HEPATIC ANATOMY
Smooth Two-Lobed Human Liver
Showed the human liver is a smooth two-lobed organ
(right & left lobes) — no five animal lobes clasping the
stomach, and no rete mirabile in the human head.
• Encouraged fellow anatomists (Colombo, Falloppio,
Fabricius & Harvey) to question ancient texts empirically.

svg.text: EDEXCEL EXAM TAKEAWAY · WHY VESALIUS'S 1543 FABRICA WAS A LANDMARK TURNING POINT
Combining hands-on human dissection, Renaissance anatomical art, and the printing press, Vesalius broke the 1,400-year stranglehold
of Galenic dogma and established direct observation of the human body as the foundation of modern medical science.
